exercise_description: While working on a branch, I initiated a merge.
I am presented with merge prompt screen, but now I wish to abort the operation.
hints: Read the instructions on the merge prompt screen carefully.
What happens if you close the terminal window without any changes ?
What happens if you delete the commit message ?

checks.name: Check commit message
explanation: Check that the user has closed the editor with the commit message prompt.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of git merge commits.
checks.command: test -z "$(git lg | grep "Merge branch 'feat' - Git Master (HEAD -> main)")"

exercise_description: I worked on a feature and I wanted to rebase my branch upon main,
But instead I accidentally did a merge.
I want to the merge and have a linear history.
hints: Use 'git lg' to check the history of the commits.
Be careful not to loose any files, or any commits
Git reflog is a trap
Try resetting your HEAD~1

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of git merge commits.

checks.name: Check files
explanation: Check that are all files are present in the working tree.
checks.command: for f in file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt; do [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "Missing $f"; exit 1; }; done

checks.name: Check commits
explanation: Check all three commits are present 'first', 'second' and 'third'

exercise_description: I edited the text1.txt file
I want to rebase my feat branch onto main
But another user edited the same file on main
hints: When conflicts occur during rebase, git will pause and show you the conflicted files.
Edit the conflicted files to resolve merge conflicts manually.
After resolving conflicts, use 'git add' to mark files as resolved.
Continue the rebase process with 'git rebase --continue'.
If you want to abort the rebase, use 'git rebase --abort'.

checks.name: Check commit history
explanation: After rebasing all commits should be present in the history
checks.command: for s in "I too edited file1" "edited file1"; do git log --pretty=%s | grep -Fxq "$s" || { echo "Missing commit: $s"; exit 1; }; done

checks.name: Check file content
explanation: The file content should contain both the text from the first and second commits

exercise_description: I accidentally committed my password to the repo
I want to completely remove any mention of my password from the history
hints: Use 'git lg' to view the commit history
On what branches is it present ?
How do you remove the commit from both local and remote branch ?
How about the git objects ?
git-filter-repo --sensitive-data-removal --replace-text password.txt --force
git push --force --mirror origin

checks.name: Check git history for password
checks.command: test $(git rev-list --objects --all | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 git cat-file -p | grep 'pa$$word' -c) -eq 0
explanation: The user should have successfully removed the commit from the history. Check the git objects to ensure that password is no longer present in git's internals.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Make sure other commits are not lost
checks.command: git lg | grep -q "some content - Git Master"

exercise_description: A colleague works on another repository that is not related to mine and have pushed a commit called 'other commit'.
I want to get the content of their commit on my repo.
I added the second repository as a remote and pulled
And I receive the following error when trying merge: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
hints: Next hint will reveal the solution
Use git merge --allow-unrelated-histories

checks.name: Check worktree files
explanation: The worktree should contain a file called 'file_other.txt' from the other remote.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: The git history should contain a commit called 'other commit' from the other remote.
checks.command: git lg | grep -q "other commit - Git Master"

exercise_description: I try to create a branch called "feat/my_feat"
But when I try to push it to the remote, it results in an error
! [remote rejected] feat/mine -> feat/mine (failed to update ref)

checks.name: Check the local branch has been pushed to remote.
explanation: Verify that the user has successfully resolved the error and pushed the branch to the remote.

hints: Is your local up-to date ?
Do a git fetch, and then git branch -a
Is there anything unusual in the branch name that came from the remote ?
Since git refs are stored as files in directory structure, having a ref called 'feat' will cause problems when we want to create a branch called 'feat/<name>'.
One solution would be to rename your local branch to feature/mine

exercise_description: I worked on a feature
And I had to quickly change a branch so I performed a "WIP" commit at one point.
I want to clean this WIP commit before opening my merge request.
hints: Be careful, git reset HEAD~2 is not a good idea.
How about interactive rebase ?
git rebase -i HEAD~3, then prefix the commit with s to squash it.
Don't forget to push --force your branch.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of the WIP commit.

checks.name: Check worktree files
explanation: Check that the file related to the WIP commit has not been lost.

exercise_description: I did a wrong checkout
Now my HEAD is in a detached state
I want to attach my HEAD to a branch so that further commits are kept
hints: Use 'git status' to see the 'detached HEAD' notice.
Simply reattach to an existing branch: git checkout main.
Avoid committing while detached or you may lose the commit reference.

checks.name: HEAD is attached to a branch
explanation: Ensure HEAD points to a branch, not a detached state.

checks.name: No commits lost
explanation: Verify that the original 'second commit' still exists in the repository graph.
